question: Autocal on imperfect machines (PR #121 follow-up). (1) A wrong configured line stiffness trades off almost perfectly against top anchor D.z with the current collection routine and force tuning; find force/compliance-tuning data that reveals the real compliance so D.z is recovered even when config.g stiffness is wrong. (2) The default fit assumes all low anchors share one height; real machines differ slightly and the current residual does not catch one wrong low-anchor z. First benchmark on randomized imperfect machines (uneven anchor heights, off-centre top anchor, ±20% compliance error), several seeds, report spread. Only then compare collection patterns. Radius variation and line buildup are out of scope. Small experiments first, then HP3, then HP4, HP5, HP5r. Use Rerun recordings sparingly.

agents.question: Imperfect-machine benchmark and baseline spread. Build a reproducible way to run the default autocal (flat circle sweeps + point fit) on randomized imperfect simulated machines: per-seed uneven low-anchor z heights (few mm to a few cm), an off-centre top anchor (XY offset), and true line compliance differing from the config.g stiffness by up to ±20%. Keep radius variation and line buildup out of scope. Report per-anchor-coordinate true error spread across several seeds (start with small/fast experiments, then HP3 only; scale to HP4/HP5/HP5r only if cheap and stable). Attribute which perturbation drives which error (e.g. stiffness error -> D.z, low-anchor z error -> ?), and whether current residual/jackknife scores flag the bad cases. The harness must be reusable by other researchers (one command per seed/machine, results JSON with truth vs fit). Do not change collection patterns.

Compliance observability for the top anchor height. With todays collection and force tuning, a wrong configured line stiffness (config.g) trades off almost perfectly against top anchor D.z (and the held-anchor z vs free-line stretch-scale degeneracy in research/output/session-2026-11-20-ellipsoid-autocal/report.md). Find force/compliance-tuning data that makes the real compliance observable so D.z is recovered even when configured stiffness is wrong by ±20%: e.g. measuring encoder length change vs commanded force at fixed poses, varying pretension along the null vector, multi-force-level sweeps, and fitting a compliance scale (or per-line EA/L) jointly with anchors. First quantify the degeneracy and the information each candidate adds with small synthetic/offline experiments, then confirm the best candidate on HP3 in the real simulator with true stiffness off by ±20%. Report D.z error and time cost. Radius variation and line buildup out of scope. Do not compare collection patterns beyond what is needed to add compliance information.

Uneven low-anchor heights. The default point fit assumes all low anchors share one z; real machines differ slightly, and the current residual/jackknife does not catch one wrong low-anchor z. Determine (a) how much anchor error a few-mm to few-cm height difference of one low anchor causes with the equal-height assumption, (b) whether per-anchor low z can be fitted identifiably from current data (and what conditioning/priors are needed, coupling with D.z and stiffness), and (c) a residual, model-comparison or diagnostic that reliably flags a wrong low-anchor z. Start with small synthetic/offline experiments on existing datasets and the pose fit, then confirm on HP3 simulated machines with one or more low anchors raised/lowered. Radius variation and line buildup out of scope. Do not compare collection patterns.

Compliance probe where stiffness really trades against the top anchor. Prior work (branch t3/top-anchor-compliance-observability, 6c9cd463; review reviews/review-78e5d2a30d57) found a wrong configured stiffness moves D.z strongly only on HP5 pulley-reduced (HP5r) default sweeps (~8.4 mm per unit k) and in the opt-in ellipsoid shape (5-10 mm per unit k on all machines), while on HP3 the home-strain term with configured stiffness gives ~95% of the gain and the probe is unneeded. Test live whether the opt-in fixed-pose compliance probe (HP_SIM5_COMPLIANCE_PROBE) recovers k and removes the top-anchor z error on HP5r sweeps and on the ellipsoid shape, at true EA x0.8 and x1.2 (several seeds each), compared with the configured-stiffness fit; also test fitting k jointly from HP5r sweep data alone (its rms had a minimum near k=1.04). Report error in the frame convention (top x=y=0), spread, and time cost. If the probe is unnecessary everywhere, say so.

Rough-bootstrap robustness on imperfect machines. HP5 pulley-reduced (HP5r) imperfect-machine seed 3 fails autocal at the rough bootstrap deterministically (both true EA x0.8 and x1.2, with or without the compliance probe), on the free-low-z fit; the old fit also failed HP5 with A raised 5 mm (unreliable-rough-bootstrap) and HP3 seed 9 hit a force auto-tune knife-edge (fixed by 1ec95e5e). Diagnose the root cause of the HP5r seed 3 bootstrap failure, fix it minimally, and check the fix does not change outcomes on the existing passing seeds and the CI-nominal machines. Then estimate the bootstrap failure rate on random imperfect machines (several seeds per machine, prioritising HP5r and HP5) before and after the fix. A run that never fails matters more than a slightly better mean.

Force realisation error in autocal data. Replays (t3/test-compliance-probe-stiffness 7bfd016c, report section 7) show torque-mode motors produce tensions off the commanded force (HP3 ellipsoid steps ~2.5% short +-0.2 N; HP5r last sweep point 0.53 N below command), and that feeding produced instead of commanded forces cuts the top-anchor z error at true stiffness by 0.6-1.0 mm on both replayed runs, more than any choice of k. Characterise the cause in the simulator (detent/cogging vs servo/torque-constant error vs saturation vs load-dependent friction), and judge which parts are likely physical on real hardware versus sim artefacts (check the motor model and the motor-saturation / phase-averaged detent notes). Then test mitigations that do not rely on knowing the sim internals: e.g. averaging over motor phase (small dithers), approaching each force level from both sides, estimating the realised force from encoder data, or a per-motor force-offset/scale parameter fitted jointly with anchors. Report the top-anchor z and max print-frame error on imperfect machines (several seeds; HP3 first, then HP5r) and time cost.

Make the home-stretch correction the default autocal fit. The compliance study (session ...-4f2510fd, branch t3/top-anchor-compliance-observability, review reviews/review-78e5d2a30d57) showed that on HP3 adding the HP4-style home-strain term (the low lines are slack at encoder zero and their measurement stretch acts as a home offset) with the configured stiffness cuts max print-frame error 1.07 -> 0.38 mm in offline refits. The human approved making it the default, starting with HP3, then HP4, HP5 and HP5r, accepting changed stored benchmark numbers. Implement it as the default in the live fit (small change, no new flags unless needed; delete superseded code), verify live on the imperfect-machine harness with the same seeds as the baseline (paired comparison, print-frame error, top-anchor z, stop reasons, time), machine by machine in that order, and only proceed to the next machine when the previous one does not regress. Also verify the stored CI benchmark (autocal/tests/test_autocal_benchmark.py) on unperturbed machines and update expected numbers if the human-approved change moves them. The opt-in compliance probe is out of scope here except as a note.

Production force-realisation fitting. Reuse blind period scan and force contrasts where justified. Test HP5r and the default HP3 home-strain path on held-out and high-ripple data, quantify cost and regressions, and guard unsupported fits. Implement a small production path with a baseline fallback if supported by evidence.

Isolate the remaining HP5r top-anchor height bias with controlled forward/replay experiments, including effector rotation and downstream model assumptions. Implement a correction only if independently observable and validated. Perform the subsequent paired collection-pattern comparison with the current robust model when feasible; preserve negative outcomes, coordinate any dependency on the force-fit lane.
